title: MRI learning distinguishes histories of suicide attempt in bipolar depression
summary: A two-level nearest-neighbor classifier used dynamic resting-state MRI features to distinguish bipolar-depression patients with a recent suicide-attempt history. After development in 176 patients, an additional 33-patient cohort yielded 72.72% accuracy. This is retrospective classification of an assessed clinical history, rather than prospective prediction of future attempts. Small external numbers, feature-selection optimism and clinical utility remain limitations.

source_review.scope: Primary relevant Methods/results/limitations, exact primary front identity and current primary PubMed notice metadata; version dates distinguished.

evidence.tested: Patient-level classification, permutation checks and an additional 33-patient cohort with psychiatrist-assessed attempt histories.
evidence.unknown: Future-event prediction, causal brain mechanisms and clinical management benefit remain unestablished; internal supervised feature selection may be optimistic.
evidence.ai_role: A first nearest-neighbor stage selects informative dynamic-activity voxels, and a second combines their features to classify assessed attempt histories.
